title.narrative: Community-led solutions for addressing climate-induced migration & resilience in the Sundarbans

description.narrative: The Sundarbans region of Bangladesh, the world's largest mangrove forest, is home to communities that are increasingly vulnerable to climate change. Rising sea levels, more frequent and powerful cyclones, the river erosion of agricultural land and saline intrusion are damaging health and livelihood security. The most marginalised groups (women and young people) are disproportionately affected. One of the most prevalent coping strategies is migration but this has a negative impacts on the individual and the families staying behind. Migrants often experience a range of exploitative practices including unsafe working conditions, withheld pay, limited social protection and restricted rights and services. Their families can also become more vulnerable owing to disrupted education and reduced parental care. This project tackles these issues through (i) awareness raising and community engagement activities designed to increase understanding of climate and migration risks; (ii) provide life skills training to build resilience, enhance adaptation to living in a saline environment, and connect eligible families to government social support schemes; (iii) provide vocational/technical training to increase livelihood options; and (iv) foster local youth leadership to plan and implement adaptation strategies. Finally, OKUP will use the evidence generated by the project to contribute to their policy and advocacy work, publishing articles/papers and attending national/ international events on climate induced migration issues.
